title: Python script + skill: validate docs/tasks/ JSON structure
description: User request: a Python script for validating docs/tasks/ JSON structure, plus a skill wrapping it. Implement a validator checking every docs/tasks/*.json and docs/tasks/done/*.json against the invariants CLAUDE.md's 'Task board' section documents: the required top-level shape (id, title, area, skill, state, depends_on, references, description, checklist, and the optional decisions/questions/git/test/review/pr_decision fields when present) and each field's type; `state` is one of the five documented values; each checklist item has `step` (string) and `done` (boolean); each `decisions` entry has `decision`+`rationale` (plus `timestamp`/`recorded_by`) and each `questions` entry has `question`+`context` (plus `timestamp`/`raised_by`) -- a bare 'changed X' is exactly what CLAUDE.md calls out as NOT a valid decision record; every `depends_on` id actually exists somewhere on the board; `docs/tasks/index.json`'s per-task `state`/`path` exactly mirrors that task's own file (the 'mirror, not a separate source of truth' rule) with no drift; and a task's file is under `docs/tasks/done/` if and only if its `state` is `"done"` (the exact invariant CLAUDE.md calls out by name). This is a repo-wide bookkeeping concern, not backend-specific -- decide the script's location (a new top-level scripts/ vs. backend/scripts/) and whether it should be stdlib-only (so it needs no venv/install step) as part of this task, recording the choice as a decisions entry.

checklist.step: Decide the script's location and dependency footprint (prefer a new top-level scripts/ directory and stdlib-only Python, since this validates repo-wide task-board JSON, not backend application code) and record as a decisions entry.

Implement the validator per the invariants listed in this task's description, sourced from CLAUDE.md's Task board section (required fields/types, valid state values, checklist/decisions/questions entry shape, depends_on resolution, index.json mirror consistency, the done<=>docs/tasks/done/ path invariant).
Exit non-zero with a clear, per-task list of every violation found on failure; exit 0 with a brief summary on success, so it works both interactively and as a gate.

Run it once for real against the current board and report what it finds (fixing anything trivially wrong is fine; anything requiring a judgment call about board content itself is out of scope for this task -- report it instead).

Create a `.claude/skills/` entry wrapping the script (name TBD, record the actual choice), following existing skill conventions (see static-verify for a similar 'run a checker, report results' skill).
Register the new skill in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.

Decide whether to wire this validator into any existing skill/agent (e.g. as an orchestrate-tasks preflight step, or part of revalidate-done-tasks) and make that change only if it's small and clearly beneficial; record the decision either way.

decisions.decision: Placed the validator at a new top-level scripts/validate_tasks.py (not backend/scripts/), and wrote it stdlib-only (json, pathlib, sys, typing) with no dependency on anything in backend/pyproject.toml's [dev] extras.
decisions.rationale: docs/tasks/ is a repo-wide bookkeeping concern read and written by every pipeline agent (task-worker, pr-reviewer, pr-decision, pr-merger, next-task, task-qa-reviewer, orchestrate-tasks, revalidate-done-tasks), none of which are backend-application code -- backend/scripts/ (export_openapi.py, fix_schema_drift.py) is specifically for backend/app's own OpenAPI contract, and putting a task-board validator there would misleadingly imply it needs the backend venv or is scoped to backend/app. A top-level scripts/ directory (this is its first file) makes the tool runnable with a bare `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` from repo root with zero setup -- important since it's meant to be invoked from orchestrate-tasks preflight and ad hoc by any agent/human without first activating backend/.venv or running pip install. Rejected: backend/scripts/ (wrong scope, implies a backend/app dependency that doesn't exist) and depending on a JSON-schema library like jsonschema/pydantic (would need backend/.venv or a new top-level venv just to run a board lint, contradicting the zero-setup goal; stdlib json+pathlib is entirely sufficient for these invariants, which are simple presence/type/cross-reference checks, not a full recursive schema).
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered defining the schema as a JSON Schema document validated via the jsonschema package for a more declarative spec, rejected because it would reintroduce the install-step dependency this task's own description explicitly asks to avoid, for invariants (index.json mirror consistency, done<=>docs/tasks/done/ path checks, cross-file depends_on resolution) that aren't expressible in JSON Schema alone anyway and would need custom Python logic regardless.

decisions.decision: review.comments[].file and review.comments[].line are treated as valid when explicitly null, not just when a well-typed string/int or entirely absent -- only a wrong-typed non-null value is flagged.
decisions.rationale: Running the validator for real against the current ~109-task board (per this task's checklist) initially reported 28 'must be a string/integer when present' violations across 9 tasks, all on review.comments[].file/.line being explicitly null rather than a string/int. Inspecting the actual data (e.g. docs/tasks/done/confidence-scoring.json's review.comments[2]) showed this is a deliberate, widespread convention across independently-written pr-reviewer passes: a review comment that isn't pinned to one specific file/line (a suite-wide coverage note, a general methodology observation) legitimately carries file: null / line: null rather than omitting the keys. This is a bug in the validator's own type-checking (not distinguishing 'absent' from 'present but null' for an inherently optional pointer), not a defect in ~9 tasks' worth of board content, so it was fixed in the script itself rather than reported as 28 board violations -- exactly the 'fix anything trivially wrong yourself' case the checklist item calls out, as opposed to a judgment call about board content.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered instead 'fixing' the 28 occurrences in the task JSON files themselves (dropping the null keys or filling in a placeholder file/line), rejected because the null values are semantically correct (those comments genuinely have no single file/line to point at) and rewriting 9 already-reviewed/merged done tasks' historical review records to satisfy an overly strict validator would be changing accepted history to fit new tooling, backwards from what should happen.

decisions.decision: Named the wrapping skill validate-task-board (.claude/skills/validate-task-board/SKILL.md), and wired it into two existing places: a new bullet in orchestrate-tasks' Preflight section (run once before the loop, non-blocking -- fix trivial issues or note the finding and proceed, unlike the hard-blocking GitHub-auth preflight check) and a pointer added to revalidate-done-tasks step 1 (run the script as the fast first pass for the index.json mirror / done-path cross-check that step already describes doing by hand, without replacing the deeper per-task content checks in steps 2+).
decisions.rationale: 'validate-task-board' matches this project's existing verb-object skill-naming convention (check-coverage, static-verify, add-indicator) and reads unambiguously as 'validate the docs/tasks/ board' rather than something narrower like 'validate-tasks' (could be misread as validating individual checklist items' correctness, which this script doesn't do). Both wiring points are small (a few sentences each, no new control flow) and clearly beneficial: orchestrate-tasks already fails fast on a broken GitHub credential before dispatching any agent for the same reason (a systemic problem should be caught once, not rediscovered per-task) -- a corrupted board (bad JSON, an index.json drift) can misdirect next-task/task-worker for whichever task it touches, so the same fail-fast-but-narrow logic applies, except non-blocking since a single task's board defect shouldn't stall every other ready task's progress. revalidate-done-tasks' step 1 already manually performs exactly the index.json-mirror/done-path cross-check this script automates, so pointing at the script there removes duplicated manual work without changing that skill's scope or deeper per-task content checks.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered also wiring it into task-worker's or pr-reviewer's own per-task workflow (validate after every task-file edit), rejected as unnecessarily heavy for what's meant to be a lightweight, occasional board-wide health check, and out of scope for 'only make that change if it's small and clearly beneficial' -- a per-commit hook belongs to a future task's decision, not this one's. Considered naming it 'validate-tasks' to shadow the script's own filename, rejected in favor of 'validate-task-board' for the disambiguation reason above.

decisions.decision: Addressed pr-reviewer's needs_work verdict on PR #113: (1) guarded the four `x not in <set-of-strings>` membership checks (test.verdict, review.verdict, test.gap_analysis[].severity, index.json per-task state) with an `isinstance(value, str)` check first, so a non-scalar field value (list/dict) produces a normal violation message instead of an uncaught TypeError crashing the whole run -- verified by reproducing the exact `{"test": {"verdict": ["pass"]}}` case against the real board (clean report, no traceback, exit 1) and adding four dedicated regression tests. (2) Rewrote orchestrate-tasks' preflight validator step to stop telling the orchestrator to fix findings 'on the current branch (main)': it's now report-only by default (note violations, proceed with the loop) and, for the rare case a violation blocks the very next task about to be dispatched, spells out the real mechanics (dedicated branch, commit, push, `gh pr create` -- a direct board-authoring PR a human merges, mirroring revalidate-done-tasks' 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section and the #60/#91/#99 precedent) rather than implying a direct edit on `main` works. Also fixed all three non-blocking findings while in the same file/function: the dead id-vs-filename check now compares against the file's actual `path.stem` (passed into check_task_shape separately from the already-resolved task_id) instead of comparing task_id against itself; tasks_by_id now keys by id -> list of (data, path) instead of a single tuple, so a duplicate id no longer silently drops the earlier copy's depends_on/index-mirror cross-checks; and added a persisted, stdlib-only regression suite at scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py (23 tests: every violation category on synthetic fixtures, all four non-scalar-crash cases, the duplicate-id cross-check case, and a real-board clean-pass smoke test) runnable via `python3 scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py` with no venv/pytest needed, matching the validator's own zero-setup philosophy.
decisions.rationale: The four crash sites all shared the exact same root cause pr-reviewer identified (a bare `not in <set>` requires the left operand to be hashable, so a JSON list/dict raises TypeError instead of failing the intended type check) -- fixing all four together, plus auditing the rest of the file for the same pattern (found none: every other membership/equality check either already isinstance-guards first, as the pre-existing `state not in VALID_STATES` check at the top-level did, or uses `!=`/`==` which never raises regardless of operand type, e.g. pr_decision.verdict's `!= "merge"` comparison), closes the whole class of bug rather than just the four reviewer-named instances. For the orchestrate-tasks fix, choosing 'report-only, no auto-fix' over 'auto-fix via a real branch/PR' (the other option the review comment offered) keeps the preflight step lightweight and matches its own stated non-blocking intent (a validator finding on one task's JSON already 'shouldn't stall every other ready task' per the pre-existing wording) -- teaching the orchestrator to open its own ad hoc board-authoring PR mid-preflight for every run would add meaningful process weight for a step that's explicitly meant to be fast and low-stakes; the branch/PR mechanics are still spelled out for the one case (blocking the very next dispatch) where a fix genuinely can't just wait. The three non-blocking fixes were done now rather than deferred to scripts-validate-tasks-followups because they were small, in the exact file/function already being touched for the two blocking fixes, and (per the followups task's own text) a committed regression suite would have caught the two blocking bugs in the first place -- writing that suite now, while the crash bug is fresh, is more valuable than writing it later against code that's already drifted.
decisions.alternatives_considered: For the non-scalar crash fix, considered a single shared `expect_str_in(value, valid_set, field_name)` helper used at all four (and future) sites instead of four separate inline isinstance guards; rejected for this PR to keep the diff minimal and closely mirror the review comment's own suggested fix ('the same pattern already used correctly for the top-level state check') -- a shared helper is a reasonable follow-up but not required to close the bug. For the regression-test follow-up, considered adding it under backend/tests/ instead (this repo's existing pytest suite) or as `scripts/test_validate_tasks.py` directly; rejected backend/tests/ because that suite requires backend/.venv and is scoped to backend/app per CLAUDE.md's Backend environment notes, which would misleadingly imply this repo-wide board validator needs the backend venv to be tested (the same reasoning already recorded above for why the validator itself isn't under backend/scripts/); put it in a new scripts/tests/ subdirectory rather than flat in scripts/ so test discovery (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`) doesn't require distinguishing test files from tool files by naming convention alone as the scripts/ directory grows.

comments.summary: BLOCKING: scripts/validate_tasks.py crashes with an uncaught TypeError instead of reporting a violation when a checked field is a non-scalar (list/dict) rather than the expected string. `test["verdict"] not in VALID_TEST_VERDICTS` (and the same pattern at review.verdict, test.gap_analysis[].severity, and index.json's per-task state) calls `not in` on a set of strings, which raises `TypeError: unhashable type` if the value is a list/dict rather than being caught gracefully. Reproduced directly: a task file with `"test": {"verdict": ["pass"]}` makes the whole script abort with a traceback instead of printing `FAIL: N violation(s) found`. This defeats the tool's entire purpose -- gracefully reporting exactly this class of malformed data -- and would break the non-interactive preflight use in orchestrate-tasks/revalidate-done-tasks (a crash there looks like a script bug, not an actionable board finding). Fix: guard each of these four `not in <set>` checks with an `isinstance(value, str)` check first, the same pattern already used correctly for the top-level `state` check at line 106.

BLOCKING: .claude/skills/orchestrate-tasks/SKILL.md's new preflight step tells the orchestrator to "fix anything trivially wrong on the current branch (`main`, since nothing has been dispatched yet) and re-run the validator" for a validator finding. This is unworkable as written: CLAUDE.md states explicitly (and this file's own diff references) that "main's branch-protection ruleset rejects every direct push, including a bookkeeping-only one" -- so a fix made directly on `main` can never actually be pushed upstream. If the instruction instead means editing-but-not-committing, that leaves uncommitted changes on `main` in the shared working tree, which CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time on the shared working tree' section warns against (a subsequent task-worker branch cut from `main` would pick up those uncommitted edits). Either reading breaks. Fix: the instruction needs a real persistence path for a trivial board fix -- e.g. open a small dedicated PR for the fix (same as any other change to `main`), or explicitly scope 'fix' to only editing the in-memory/dispatch-time understanding without touching tracked files, and say so.

Non-blocking: scripts/validate_tasks.py's own 'id field does not match its filename' check is dead code -- run() computes `task_id = data["id"] if is_nonempty_str(data.get("id")) else path.stem` and passes that same task_id into check_task_shape, whose internal comparison `data["id"] != task_id` can therefore never be true whenever `id` is a nonempty string. Verified by hand: a scratch task file with a mismatched `id` vs. filename produced zero violation for this rule. Not one of the invariants the task's own description lists as required, and none of those are affected (all independently verified working via synthetic negative cases). Filed as a tracked follow-up (scripts-validate-tasks-followups) rather than blocking on its own, but should be fixed alongside the two blocking items above since they're in the same function/file.

Non-blocking: no persisted/committed regression test for scripts/validate_tasks.py itself -- the synthetic negative-case smoke test mentioned in the PR summary was apparently ad hoc and not committed, so there's no automated way to re-verify the validator's own correctness going forward (and a committed test would likely have caught both blocking findings above). Filed as a tracked follow-up.

Non-blocking: scripts/validate_tasks.py's `tasks_by_id[task_id] = (data, path)` silently overwrites an earlier entry when two task files share the same id (e.g. a stale copy left behind after an incomplete git mv to docs/tasks/done/); the duplicate is flagged once as 'duplicate id', but subsequent index.json-mirror/depends_on cross-checks then only run against whichever file was processed last. Filed as a tracked follow-up.

review.notes: Verified against CLAUDE.md's Task board section directly (not just the PR summary): the six required invariants (top-level shape/types incl. optional decisions/questions/git/test/review/pr_decision; state in the five documented values; checklist step+done shape; decisions decision+rationale shape including the literal 'bare changed X isn't a decision record' rule; questions question+context shape; depends_on resolution against the whole board; index.json state/path mirror; done<=>docs/tasks/done/ path invariant) are all correctly implemented and matched CLAUDE.md's wording when I re-read that section myself. Ran `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` for real: clean pass, 109 task files, matching the PR's claimed smoke test. Independently re-ran a synthetic negative-case test (21 distinct violations across every documented category) and confirmed each fires correctly -- except the dead id-vs-filename check (non-blocking, see below). A second independent code-review pass (code-review skill, high effort) then surfaced two further, genuinely blocking bugs I hadn't caught in my own manual pass: an uncaught TypeError crash on non-scalar field values, and a broken persistence path in the new orchestrate-tasks preflight instruction -- both reproduced directly and confirmed real, see comments. Spot-checked the review.comments[].file/.line null-handling decision against docs/tasks/done/confidence-scoring.json's review.comments[2] (file: null, line: null, a suite-wide coverage note) -- confirmed a real, legitimate existing convention, not board content that should have been 'fixed' instead; that particular validator bug fix was the right call. Both 'decide X' checklist items (script location/dependency footprint; wiring into existing skills) have corresponding decisions entries with real rationale and rejected alternatives -- no gap there. Backend: pytest --cov=app, 560 passed, 99.86% coverage (gate 90%). Frontend: vitest --coverage, 99.6%+ across all four metrics (gate 90%). Backend ruff/mypy clean; frontend eslint/tsc clean; ran ruff check against the new scripts/ directory directly too (not part of the enforced gate, same as backend/scripts/'s existing precedent) -- clean. No backend/app, frontend/, or openapi.json changes in this diff, so no OpenAPI staleness concern and no browser walkthrough/e2e run needed -- this PR has no UI surface (scripts/skills/docs/task-JSON only). architecture-review's checklist (data/indicators/signals/portfolio layering, API routers, React Query, coverage config) doesn't apply -- no app code touched, no new runtime dependency (stdlib only), docs/Architecture.md is silent on repo tooling by design. The revalidate-done-tasks wiring (a pointer to the script as a fast first pass, not replacing the deeper per-task content checks) is fine as-is; only the orchestrate-tasks wiring has the blocking issue above. Filed the three non-blocking findings as scripts-validate-tasks-followups (new task, none existed for this id yet).
